Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) between Canada and the European Union
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), in force for Canada December 30, 2018

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17, and Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Regulations, SOR/2002-184, as amended; Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, s. 21.1 (register of individuals with significant control), as amended by the federal beneficial-ownership transparency framework (Budget Implementation Act, 2023, No. 1; provisions in force January 22, 2024); Business Corporations Act (Alberta), R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9, and the Alberta Corporate Registry fee and name-search regulations; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46, Part XII.2 (proceeds of crime); Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, S.C. 1997, c. 24.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport (or national identity card) of each proposed director, officer, and individual with significant control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed notary public or law society commissioner of oaths in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Convention of 5 October 1961; in force for Canada since January 11, 2024; apostille for Alberta domestic documents issued by the Court of King's Bench of Alberta; foreign documents apostilled by the competent authority of the originating state) OR consular legalization at the competent Canadian mission where the origin state is not an Apostille party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Individual with Significant Control (UBO) declaration and ownership-attestation affidavit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Alberta lawyer authorized to administer affidavits, or foreign notary where the declarant is located abroad
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille chain for foreign execution; Alberta-issued declarations are lodged with the Alberta Corporate Registry and maintained in the corporate minute book without further authentication

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of any corporate shareholder, including registered directors and shareholders list
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Certifying corporate registry of the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the originating state's designated competent authority, or consular legalization by the Canadian embassy/consulate if the origin state is not an Apostille party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney appointing the Alberta corporate-service agent and registered-office resident
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Alberta notary public or foreign notary executing on behalf of the non-resident incorporator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for foreign execution; domestic execution by an Alberta notary requires no apostille for filing with the Alberta Corporate Registry through an authorized service provider

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds declaration for the initial capitalization contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing financial institution of the subscriber or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled or consularly legalized in the issuing state, with counterparty confirmation by the receiving Alberta financial institution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders with significant control, and counterparties against the Consolidated United Nations Security Council Sanctions List, the Canadian list of designated persons issued under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, the Office of Foreign Assets Control Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (required for USD Swift LC and TT wire clearing), and the politically exposed persons (PEP) database of the receiving Canadian financial institution; screening is required before incorporation, before opening the corporate bank account, and thereafter on a rolling basis under PCMLTFA ministerial directives and FINTRAC guidance; the risk tier is confirmed as Low_Risk_Standard for ISIC 4661 wholesale bitumen logistics, yet full UBO identification remains mandatory and cannot be waived by nominee or bearer-share arrangements.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (operated by the Alberta government, available at https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry and filed through ACRS - Alberta Corporate Registration System by authorized service providers); alternative federal route: Corporations Canada Online Filing Centre at https://www.ic.gc.ca/incorporations
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed legal names must be expressed in English and/or French characters under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), R.S.A. 2000, c. B-9, and the Alberta Corporate Registry name-search regulations; names originating in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet; the distinctive element combined with a permitted designator (Inc., Corp., Ltd., Limited, Corporation, Incorporated, or French equivalents) must not create confusion with any existing registered, reserved, or trademark-protected name in the Alberta and national NUANS index.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banker, Banking, Trust, Loan, Insurance, Assurance (require prior financial regulator license and ministerial consent)
College, Institute, University, Seminary (teaching-institution consent required)
Engineer, Engineering, Consulting Engineer (requires APEGA pre-approval)
Architect (requires prior consent of the Alberta Association of Architects)
Royal, Crown, Municipal, Federal, Provincial (require prior Alberta or Crown consent)
Pulse, Co-operative, Condominium, Mortgage, Credit Union, Telecommunication (sector-specific licensing triggers)
Canada or Canadian (require consent of the Director of Corporations Canada when used by a provincial corporation)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Where the Alberta Registrar rejects a proposed name, the applicant or its authorized corporate-services agent files a written request for reconsideration with Consumer Services Alberta (Attention: Director of Corporate Registries) within 30 days of the notice of refusal, attaching a fresh NUANS name-search report and a statement establishing distinctiveness and the applicant's lawful entitlement to use the name; if the rejection is sustained, judicial review may be sought in the Court of King's Bench of Alberta under the Judicature Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. J-2, within the applicable limitation period; alternatively, a revised name combining a new distinctive element with the bitumen-wholesale trade description may be re-filed without delay through the ACRS portal, preserving the remaining validity of the 90-day NUANS report.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for this industry, provided the corporation maintains a physical street address in Alberta that is not exclusively a post-office box, together with a titled registered-office resident or licensed agent able to accept service; a standard virtual-office or CPA agent-office arrangement in Calgary or Edmonton is regarded as acceptable commercial substance for a low-risk bitumen trading vehicle, although the receiving Canadian bank will require evidence of real business premises or a professional agency relationship and may decline a purely mailbox address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low, estimated at 5-10% probability within the first 12-month period for a Low_Risk_Standard ISIC 4661 wholesale entity; however, the risk rises to approximately 35-45% if the Alberta Corporate Registry or Canada Revenue Agency identifies irregular Swift LC or TT wire patterns, a foreign-address-only shareholder profile, or inconsistency between declared commercial substance and transactional volumes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), R.S.A. 2000, c B-9 (ABCA), ss 5-19 (incorporation), s 103 (registered office), s 101 (directors), s 106 (records office); Corporate Registry Regulation, Alta Reg 80/2020
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — Corporations and Business Registries, Service Alberta (via Corporate Registry Electronic System, CORES)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) together with Notice of Registered Office (Form 8) and Notice of Directors (Form 2)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under the ABCA. Shares may be issued with or without par value, with no escrow or pre-funded capital deposit required for incorporation. The incorporator need only subscribe for and hold at least one share.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that the shares subscribed by the incorporators, as recorded in the subscription ledger, are hereby allotted and issued, and the directors are authorized to deliver share certificates therefor. RESOLVED that the registered office is fixed at the Alberta address stated in the Notice of Registered Office, and the record office is established at the same location. RESOLVED that the following are appointed as officers: President, Secretary, and Treasurer, each to serve at the pleasure of the Board. Banking relations shall be established with depositaries selected by the Board, and all funds shall be deposited therein and signatories authorized by banking resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Reservation (NUANS) — Optional for Named Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized NUANS service providers / Corporate Registry Electronic System (CORES), Service Alberta
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If a named corporation is desired, obtain a NUANS name search report (valid for 90 days) and file the name reservation request through CORES before incorporation; alternatively, select a numbered Alberta corporation name directly from the registry. For a numbered company, proceed immediately to Articles drafting.
required_dossiers: NUANS name search report (if named company)
Proposed corporate name and corporate structure
Registered office address description
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused or determined confusingly similar, submit a revised NUANS report and updated name reservation; no penalty attaches to the resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation and Mandatory Notices
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporator and corporate counsel (pre-filing step; no agency approval required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft Articles of Incorporation specifying the authorized share structure, any restrictions, and special provisions under ABCA s 6. Complete Form 8 (Notice of Registered Office) and Form 2 (Notice of Directors); obtain signed consent from each first director and ensure at least one director is an individual ordinarily resident in Canada. Execute the Articles by the incorporator.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation
Completed Form 8 — Notice of Registered Office
Completed Form 2 — Notice of Directors
Signed consent of each first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correctly revise and re-execute any deficient form; the registry will accept a cured filing without the need to restart the entire incorporation application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Incorporation Application and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry — CORES online filing portal or Service Alberta registry counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Articles of Incorporation, Notice of Registered Office and Notice of Directors through CORES or at a Service Alberta registry counter. Pay the CAD $150 incorporation filing fee plus any applicable expedited fee. Upon verification and approval, the registry issues the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Completed Articles of Incorporation
Form 8 — Notice of Registered Office
Form 2 — Notice of Directors
Filing fee payment (CAD $150) via corporate account, credit card or registry debit
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry queries the filing, respond with a corrective clarification or amendment within the registry's stated deadline, typically 14 days; expedited correction is available for an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Corporate Database Update
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After approval, download or retrieve the Certificate of Incorporation and the official corporate summary from CORES. Verify the incorporation date, Alberta entity number, director information and registered office details. Order certified copies where required for banking, land registration or trade counterparty due diligence.
required_dossiers: Application reference number or CORE transaction ID
Certificate of Incorporation (downloadable)
Corporate summary printout from CORES
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If errors appear on the certificate or corporate summary, submit an Application for Correction of Records with supporting evidence to the Corporate Registry; registry correction is ministerial in nature.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Business Number and Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the corporation with the CRA through Business Registration Online to obtain a nine-digit Business Number (BN), a corporate income tax account, and a GST/HST account (compulsory when annual taxable supplies exceed CAD $30,000, or voluntary immediately). Open a payroll deductions account if employees are engaged. For wholesale bitumen/asphalt supplies, verify the applicable GST/HST treatment including zero-rating or reverse charge rules as relevant to the specific supply stream.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Notice of Registered Office
Full legal names, addresses, dates of birth and Social Insurance Numbers of directors
Description of principal business activity (NAICS 424720)
Corporate mailing address and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA registration is delayed or queried, resubmit the application with clarified business activity descriptions or contact the CRA Business Registration telephone service; request a formal taxpayer resolution where the delay persists.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Minute Book and Officer Appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's registered office and board of directors (internal step)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass unanimous written resolutions in lieu of a meeting under ABCA s 114. Adopt Bylaw No. 1, approve the pro-forma first board resolution covering share allotment, registered office adoption and officer appointments, appoint an auditor or waive the audit requirement, approve the corporate seal, establish the minute book, and authorize banking signatories.
required_dossiers: Executed pro-forma First Board Resolution
Bylaw No. 1 (adopted and executed)
Minute book and share certificate ledger
Consent to act as auditor or signed waiver of auditor appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Rectify any procedural defect by a supplementary unanimous written resolution; internal governance corrections do not require a registry filing unless the ABCA expressly so mandates.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business Licence and Commercial Bank Account Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipal licensing office (City of Edmonton or City of Calgary as applicable) and designated Canadian Schedule I bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the municipal business licence applicable to petroleum products wholesale and warehousing. Ensure compliance with the Alberta Traffic Safety Act and the federal Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act and Regulations for drummed or bagged bitumen storage. Open the corporate bank account by presenting the Certificate of Incorporation, the first board resolution, the register of directors and beneficial ownership declarations; configure SWIFT LC and TT wire payment rails in accordance with the bank's AML/KYC and EFT policy.
required_dossiers: Municipal business licence application
Certificate of Incorporation and corporate summary
Register of directors and beneficial ownership information
First board resolution on banking signatories
TDG compliance documentation for dangerous goods storage or transport
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Remediate bank KYC deficiencies by providing further source-of-funds and beneficial ownership documentation. If the municipal licence is refused, appeal to the municipal development officer or apply for a variance under the applicable municipal bylaw.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No provincial industrial manufacturing licence is required for wholesale distribution of drummed and bagged penetration grade bitumen; Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) is the conditional environmental regulator for storage and handling, and the local municipal licensing office is the competent authority for premises-based business licensing.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal Business Licence (Wholesale / Petroleum Products Storage and Distribution) and, where applicable, a Transportation of Dangerous Goods (TDG) certificate for the handling of dangerous goods

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, R.S.A. 2000, c E-3 (EPEA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration (prescribed activity) without a full Environmental Impact Assessment report; a full EIA is not mandatory for wholesale trading operations lacking major industrial installations. Any petroleum storage tank system exceeding applicable regulatory thresholds requires registration or approval under the Storage and Transfer of Petroleum Products Regulation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: VOC control per the Storage and Transfer of Petroleum Products Regulation limits; wastewater discharge regulated under EPEA approvals and municipal sewer bylaws; drummed and containerized waste handling must comply with Alberta's Recycling Regulation and hazardous waste manifest requirements; all bitumen/asphalt containers must meet TDG-compliant UN packaging; Canadian Environmental Protection Act, 1999 reporting thresholds apply where toxic substance releases exceed prescribed limits.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and inspection under the Alberta Fire Code for warehouse premises; building occupancy permit and structural load clearance from the municipal development authority; Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) compliance clearance for employees; WHMIS/GHS training and emergency response planning for hazardous materials handling; workers' compensation account clearance with WCB-Alberta; municipal business licence occupancy inspection.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC), the national tax administration responsible for federal corporate income tax and GST/HST, and (under the Canada-Alberta tax collection agreement) for Alberta provincial corporate income tax. Primary portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses/business-account.html), Business Registration Online (BRO) and the new CRA business registration service, together with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) export reporting systems (Canadian Export Reporting System and related CBSA portals).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step-by-step SOP for a foreign entity establishing a tax identity for an ISIC 4661 export wholesale operation in Alberta: (1) Obtain or confirm the Alberta extra-provincial registration through the Alberta Corporate Registry so the foreign corporation is lawfully carrying on business in Alberta; (2) Apply to CRA for the statutory Business Number (BN), a 9-digit tax identifier, using Form RC1 (Application for a Business Number) filed online via Business Registration Online or by mail; the application should request the RT program account for GST/HST and the RC program account for corporate income tax; because Alberta corporate income tax is administered by the CRA, no separate provincial TIN is required; (3) If the entity is a non-resident corporation without a permanent establishment or physical presence, designate an authorized Canadian representative or agent for service and file the CRA non-resident registration package; (4) Register with the CBSA as an exporter for filing B13A / Canada Export Declaration, and open a Canadian-dollar settlement account with a Schedule I bank (or a recognized foreign branch) to receive Swift LC and TT Wire proceeds; (5) If the exporter will claim input tax credits on zero-rated exports, complete the voluntary GST/HST registration election under ETA s. 240 even if below the small supplier threshold; (6) No minimum capital, no statutory license, and no bonding requirement attach to this wholesale commodity trading activity in Alberta.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a federal or Alberta business corporation (CA_CORP, ELF 8615) is treated as a separate entity-level taxpayer: resident in Canada under Income Tax Act s. 250(4) if incorporated in Canada, and liable for Part I federal corporate income tax (15% general federal rate) plus Alberta Part 4 corporate tax (8% general rate, 2% small business rate where eligible), both assessed on worldwide income subject to foreign tax credits; no partnership-style pass-through is available to the corporation. Territorial scope note: income is allocated to Alberta for provincial tax purposes using an agreed statutory apportionment formula where the corporation has establishments both inside and outside Alberta. No tax-exempt zone applies in Alberta or Canada; only targeted incentive regimes (e.g., SR&ED, investment tax credits, and certain Alberta Crown incentive agreements) can reduce tax. Non-resident shareholders are subject to Part XIII withholding tax on dividends from this corporation: statutory 25%, reduced under applicable treaty (e.g., 5% for significant shareholdings and 15% for portfolio dividends under Canada-US Treaty Article 10).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a check-the-box classification regime. The statutory elections and designations relevant to a bitumen/asphalt trading corporation are: (a) ETA s. 156 GST/HST non-application election for taxable supplies between closely related corporations to eliminate GST leakage on intercompany logistics, storage, and financing; (b) voluntary GST/HST registration election under ETA s. 240 for zero-rated exporters, enabling input tax credit recovery for Canadian freight, warehousing, and container-handling costs; (c) ITA s. 219 branch tax parity election, relevant only if a non-resident parent operates a Canadian branch rather than the local corporation; (d) ITA foreign affiliate designations and s. 93 election where the Canadian wholesaler holds foreign selling affiliates; and (e) hybrid mismatch analysis under the BEPS Multilateral Instrument and bilateral treaty entitlement rules, under which a fiscally transparent foreign entity (e.g., a US LLC) may be disregarded for Canadian treaty benefits, but the Canadian corporation itself has no elective entity-classification mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST — federal Value-Added Tax (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act (ETA). Alberta is a non-participating province, so no Alberta provincial sales tax and no HST component applies; the headline rate of 5% GST applies to taxable supplies made in Canada, including domestic wholesale supply of petroleum bitumen.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — the small supplier threshold for GST/HST registration, computed as worldwide taxable supplies (including zero-rated exports and foreign sales) in the immediately preceding four calendar quarters plus the current quarter; a non-resident carrying on business in Canada or soliciting orders in Canada must register once this threshold is exceeded and charge GST/HST on Canadian domestic supplies; certain non-residents making taxable supplies of Canadian real property must register regardless of threshold; a zero-rated export-only trader may register voluntarily under ETA s. 240 even below the threshold to obtain input tax credits and recover GST paid on Canadian inputs.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, and no universal e-invoicing mandate currently applies in Canada. CRA requires electronic filing of GST/HST returns by all registrants with annual worldwide taxable supplies above CAD 1,000,000 (threshold lowered from CAD 1,500,000 for reporting periods ending after 2021), and requires that net tax remittances exceeding CAD 10,000 be remitted electronically. API and EDI integration is available through CRA digital services (GST/HST NETFILE, third-party software, and the GST/HST Internet File Transfer service). Separately, the CBSA requires electronic filing of export declarations (B13A / Canada Export Declaration) through the Canadian Export Reporting System for export shipments; no national clear-the-invoice type mandate exists.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating eligibility under ETA Schedule VI, Part V for drummed/bagged penetration-grade bitumen sold by the Canadian wholesale corporation to non-resident buyers: (i) common-carrier export — the supplier sells to a non-resident and the goods are delivered to a common carrier (truck, rail, ocean, or air) for export from Canada, with exportation occurring as soon as is reasonably possible (CRA generally expects export within 60 days of delivery); (ii) recipient-export — the goods are made available to the non-resident buyer and are actually exported by the buyer within a reasonable time; (iii) non-resident export within 12 months — goods in Canada for less than 12 months before being exported by a non-resident person, applicable to containerized inventory held in Canadian transit hubs or temporary consignment warehouses; and (iv) zero-rated services — trading, logistics, marketing, and freight-forwarding services supplied to the non-resident buyer are zero-rated under ETA Schedule VI, Part V, s. 7 as services supplied to a non-resident person, subject to carve-outs for services performed in Canada in connection with Canadian real property or tangible personal property or supplied to individuals present in Canada. The exporter must hold contemporaneous records proving the goods left Canada and reached the destination market; GST paid on export freight, drayage, terminal handling, and storage is recoverable as input tax credits under ETA s. 169 only where the exporter is a GST/HST registrant.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (B13A / Canada Export Declaration filed electronically via the Canadian Export Reporting System, containing the exporter Business Number, H.S. 2713.20 classification for petroleum bitumen, customs value, destination country, and shipment particulars)
Bill of Lading (ocean, rail, or truck B/L with the Canadian port or rail exit, foreign discharge or destination point, shipment date, and INCO term)

Inward Remittance Certificate (bank-generated proof of inward remittance, e.g., SWIFT MT103 / TT credit advice, evidencing receipt of export proceeds in the Canadian corporate account from the non-resident buyer)
Commercial invoice and weight/quantity packing list for drummed and bagged bitumen (container count, gross/net weight, unit price, H.S. code, and delivery terms)
Sales contract or letter of credit (Swift LC) identifying the non-resident buyer, delivery terms, and transfer of title and risk outside Canada
Customs broker export summary, carrier container release or rail waybill, and, where available, the destination market customs entry evidencing arrival at the foreign port or bonded facility
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The export zero-rating file is a CRA priority audit area for commodity traders (GST/HST Memoranda and Policy P-222). Where the documentary bundle is incomplete, the transactions are circular, or the goods never leave Canada, CRA will re-characterize the supply as taxable domestically and assess: (1) GST/HST at 5% on the full selling price plus arrears interest under ETA s. 280.1 (prescribed daily compound interest); (2) a false-statement penalty under ETA s. 285(1) equal to the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the tax sought to be evaded for each false or misleading statement made knowingly or under circumstances of gross negligence; (3) additional penalties under ETA s. 280 and, for income tax, ITA s. 163(2) gross-negligence penalties equal to 50% of the understated tax; (4) criminal tax evasion charges under ETA s. 327 and Criminal Code fraud, with fines ranging from 50% to 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment up to five years; (5) retrospective clawback and reassessment within the normal four-year period, extended to ten years where misrepresentation is attributable to neglect, carelessness, or wilful default, including reversal of zero-rating, denial of input tax credits, and immediate collection of net tax, penalties, and interest; and (6) personal liability of directors and officers under ETA s. 323 and ITA s. 227.1 for unremitted GST/HST and payroll amounts. To mitigate exposure, the exporter should treat the 180-day proceeds-repatriation benchmark and the full export document bundle as a compliance floor, retain records for at least six years, and maintain a reconciliation of each container export to bank remittances and destination-market customs entries.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); foreign exchange monitoring and AML/ATF supervision fall under FINTRAC and OSFI, with no dedicated central bank exchange control branch.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current and capital account convertibility under the OECD liberalisation codes. There is no foreign exchange control, no restriction on the acquisition of CAD/USD, and no advance approval for profit remittance, dividend distribution, royalty or intercompany repayments. Non-resident shareholders are subject to Part XIII withholding tax on dividends and certain payments (generally 25% unless reduced by treaty), and the remitting company must issue an NR4 statement. Convertibility of CAD to USD is unconstrained; banks apply standard negotiated spreads and deal at prevailing market rates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender rules, conversion ratios, or repatriation deadlines in Canada. Proceeds may remain in foreign currency, be routed through a Canadian financial institution, or be converted at commercial bank rates. That said, any electronic funds transfer (EFT) of CAD 10,000 or more into or out of Canada must be reported to FINTRAC in accordance with PCMLTFA; physical import/export of currency or bearer monetary instruments exceeding CAD 10,000 must be declared to the Canada Border Services Agency at the border.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium for ancillary payments, Low for primary capital escrow or settlement accounts. Offshore digital banks and e-money institutions (EMIs) cannot accept Canadian deposits or provide a banking licence; if they provide virtual payment services in Canada, they must register as a Money Service Business (MSB) with FINTRAC and, depending on products, obtain a money transfer license from a Canadian province or be exempt as foreign remittance companies. An EMI offering CAD-denominated account equivalents without Canadian registration is inadmissible. For corporate treasury in Alberta, a Tier 1 bank account is the only reliable rail for escrow, trade settlements and FX hedging.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors or authorized officers are generally required to attend an in-person identity verification session (branch meeting in Calgary or Edmonton) or, in the alternative, comply with enhanced CDD procedures: remote identity verification by a commissioner for oaths, certified passport copies, notarized beneficial ownership declarations, live video interview and a Canadian bank reference. Most Tier 1 banks in Alberta will require at least one signing director with physical appearance for initial account opening, because the entity holds no prior bank relationship and exhibits cross-border trade activity. Remote opening is permissible only after a bank compliance committee approves an enhanced due diligence plan and the bank's CDD platform verifies the individual through refreshed biometric or credential analysis.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No local office or operating substance beyond a registered Canadian address
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Alberta corporate certificate and extra-provincial registration (if applicable), board minutes confirming business purpose, registered agent/office service agreement, transaction pipeline and sales contracts, warehouse/storage and freight forwarding agreements, insurance certificates, and audited equity injection evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner or director based in an OFAC/UK/EU sanctioned or high-risk jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced CDD form, certified passport and proof of residence, individual and entity sanctions-screening reports from Global Affairs Canada and OFAC, negative press/FATF watchlist search, declaration under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, and an independent legal opinion confirming no direct/indirect sanctions nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) or close associate appears in the shareholding or management chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP declaration executed under oath; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements backed by bank statements, audit reports, tax returns and asset valuations; notarized corporate chart; compliance committee approval and heightened ongoing monitoring consent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Containerized bitumen trade flows with BFTA or OFAC-screened destination risks and TBML red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full commercial traceability: purchase contracts and invoices incorporating HS 2713.20, container bills of lading with on-board stamps, packing lists, port/terminal surveyors' certificates (SGS/Inspectorate), quality certificates, customs declarations, freight invoices, UCP600-compliant documentary presentations, pricing evidence from Platts/Argus, and tailored end-user and jurisdiction-screening reports.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity injections are executed by the non-resident parent or shareholder via SWIFT MT103 from a regulated commercial bank to the Canadian corporate account. The standard routing is: originating bank -> SWIFT network -> Canadian bank's correspondent (e.g., RBC's New York correspondent for USD) -> receiving account. For CAD payments, LVTS provides real-time gross settlement; for USD payments, Fedwire/CHIPS settlement through New York. Remittance instructions must include: purpose code 'FDIN' (financial direct investment) or 'INTC' (intercompany funds), a reference to the subscription agreement or shareholder resolution, and the invoice/corporate account identifier. The Canadian bank will verify the source of funds and may require a board resolution, signed authority matrix, certificate of incorporation, and a source-of-wealth questionnaire before the financing activities can commence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for bitumen/asphalt trade settlements are executed through: (i) SWIFT MT103 direct telegraphic transfer (TT) for open-account and prepayment structures; (ii) documentary collections under MT400/MT422 on D/P or D/A terms; (iii) commercial letters of credit (L/C) issued via SWIFT MT700 under UCP600, with advising, confirmation, and negotiation through a bank in the seller's country; and (iv) standby L/C in MT760 as performance security. For containerized freight, documentation includes a full set of clean, on-board container bills of lading, standard commercial invoice, packing list, third-party inspection certificates, and certificate of origin. Payment debits flow through Canadian bank's LVTS for CAD and CHIPS/Fedwire for USD. Harmonized description 'penetration/contractor-grade bitumen, HS 2713.20' is recommended to avoid documentary discrepancy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR) with settlement at a future date
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) for currencies with no deliverable local foreign exchange market, contracted on an ISDA basis
Cross-currency interest-rate swap (CCS / CIRS) for asynchronous revenue and financing currencies
FX option collar and participating forward structures
Combined FX swap / swap-point rollover for intra-month liquidity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (Form AR-1) filed under section 115 of the Alberta Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 500; failure to file for two consecutive years authorizes administrative strike-off from the Alberta corporate register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal T2 Corporation Income Tax Return together with Alberta Corporate Income Tax Return (AT1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA), jointly administered with Alberta Treasury Board and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the end of each taxation year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance owing plus 1% per complete month up to 12 months; minimum CAD 1,000 where gross revenue exceeds CAD 100,000; daily compounding prescribed interest on arrears.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return for annual filers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the GST/HST reporting period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of net tax owing plus 1% per month up to 12 months; daily compounding prescribed interest on unpaid net tax.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CBCA Federal Annual Return and Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) confirmation, applicable only if the corporation is federally incorporated under the Canada Business Corporations Act instead of the Alberta ABCA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary date of federal incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing charge up to CAD 100; failure to file annual returns for two consecutive years may result in administrative dissolution by the Director.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold compels an audit for a private non-reporting Alberta corporation under the ABCA. An independent audit is mandatory for reporting issuers and corporations offering securities to the public. Shareholders holding at least 5% of voting shares may require an audit; otherwise shareholders may annually waive appointment of an auditor. Lenders or the CRA may separately impose audited financial statements as a condition.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Publicly accountable enterprises must apply IFRS (CPA Canada Handbook Part I). Private non-reporting corporations in Alberta may elect either IFRS or Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II) applied consistently; both are accepted for T2 and AT1 filing purposes.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Alberta ABCA, share transfers must be recorded in the register of members without undue delay after director approval, and the annual return confirms current directors and registered office only. Alberta does not currently require a standalone annual UBO filing for standard private ABCA corporations. For CBCA federal corporations, a register of individuals with significant control (25% or more of shares, votes, or de facto control) must be maintained and confirmed in the federal annual return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders) and share transfer records
Minute Book containing minutes of meetings and resolutions
Register of Individuals with Significant Control (required for CBCA federal corporations)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150–450 per year (CAD 200–600) for a registered office and corporate agent in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000–15,000 for a certified audit of a wholesale bitumen trading corporation; USD 1,500–4,500 for a review engagement or compilation where shareholders validly waive the full audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined: 15% federal general corporate rate + 8% Alberta general corporate rate. Qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs) may use the small business reduced rate of 11% on the first CAD 500,000 of active business income (9% federal + 2% provincial).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to ISIC 4661 wholesale supply of drummed/bagged bitumen. Effective tax can be reduced through accelerated capital cost allowance, scientific research and experimental development (SR&ED) credits, clean-technology investment tax credits, Alberta Innovation Employment Grant, and normal deductions/reserves. Losses may be carried forward 20 years and back 3 years.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return, filed via CRA E-File/Netfile, CRA My Business Account, or approved tax software. Alberta corporate income tax is calculated on the T2 provincial schedule and administered by CRA on behalf of Alberta.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual fiscal period (normally 12 months, maximum 53 weeks); quarterly tax instalments may be required when tax payable exceeds prescribed thresholds.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return due within six months after fiscal year-end. Tax balance due within two months after year-end, except qualifying CCPCs claiming the small business deduction may pay within three months. Non-resident corporations carrying on business in Canada through a permanent establishment follow the same deadlines for Canadian-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal period end, tax year length, and jurisdiction of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Canadian fiscal year-end and country of tax residence; disclose treaty jurisdiction and Alberta permanent establishment details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total wholesale revenues from bitumen, asphalt, drummed/bagged product sales, container logistics and freight recovery.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only revenue attributable to the Alberta permanent establishment; separately disclose intercompany revenue with non-arm's-length non-resident parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: opening inventory, purchases of penetration-grade bitumen, drums/bags, freight, customs duties, and closing inventory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use arm's-length cost basis; attach transfer-pricing schedules and contemporaneous documentation if any purchase or sale is with a non-arm's-length non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss before taxes, reconciled to accounting income prepared under IFRS or ASPE.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Adjust foreign-source income out of the taxable computation where not attributable to the Canadian permanent establishment; include only Canadian-source business income and taxable capital gains.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after non-capital loss carryovers, capital cost allowance, reserves, and other adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents compute taxable income on business income allocated to Alberta and net taxable capital gains attributable to the permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal Part I corporate income tax payable after foreign tax credits, investment tax credits, and other federal credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only credits specifically available to non-resident corporations and attach treaty-based computations for reduced liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta corporate tax at 8% applied to provincial taxable income, allocated under the T2 provincial allocation formula.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate Alberta taxable income using statutory gross revenue and employee remuneration factors when the non-resident has an Alberta permanent establishment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per complete month, up to 12 months; repeated late filing within 3 years: 10% plus 2% per month, up to 20 months. Failure to file information returns such as T106: CAD 100 per day, minimum CAD 100 and maximum CAD 2,500. Arrears interest accrues daily at the prescribed rate; false or neglectful statements can trigger additional civil penalties under sections 163.2 and 239 of the Income Tax Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act on dividends paid by a Canadian resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder; Alberta imposes no separate dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke reduced withholding under an income tax treaty, the non-resident beneficial owner must submit a completed CRA Form NR301 declaration to the Canadian payer before payment. The payer should also obtain a current Certificate of Residence (TRC) issued by the non-resident's home-country tax authority. Without a valid NR301 or TRC, the payer must withhold at the 25% domestic Part XIII rate. Treaty relief is claimed at source; if excess withholding occurred, the non-resident may file a Canadian non-resident tax return (NR7/R) for a refund.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Canada's statutory Part XIII withholding tax is 25% for interest and 25% for royalties. Treaty reductions can apply: under the Canada-United States treaty, arm's-length interest is generally exempt (0%), patent/trademark royalties are 10%, and certain cultural copyright royalties are 0%; many other Canadian DTAs provide interest rates of 0%-15% and royalty rates of 5%-15%. Alberta does not apply a separate provincial withholding tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada has no standalone statutory Local File/Master File monetary threshold; contemporaneous transfer-pricing documentation is required for all cross-border non-arm's-length transactions. Form T106 is mandatory when the aggregate value of reportable non-arm's-length transactions with a non-resident exceeds CAD 50,000 in the fiscal year; CRA expects full OECD-aligned documentation, including a transfer-pricing policy and benchmarking study, proportionate to the risk.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) in the offshore-centre sense are not applicable to Alberta, Canada. Canada instead applies the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (Income Tax Act section 245), transfer-pricing rules (section 247), and the central-management-and-control residency test to deny treaty benefits or reassess transactions where the corporate structure lacks real economic substance, employees, premises, or risk-bearing control.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion – False Invoicing or Misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly understating wholesale bitumen revenues, inflating cost of sales through fake supplier invoices, omitting drummed/bagged product sales, or destroying records of containerized asphalt transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act section 239(1): summary conviction carries a fine of 50% to 200% of the tax evaded and up to 2 years imprisonment; indictment carries a higher fine and up to 5 years imprisonment. CRA also reassesses the full tax, penalties, and compounded daily interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who direct or participate in false filings may be jointly and severally liable for civil restitution, assessed personally under section 227.1 for unremitted source deductions; courts can impose travel bans and imprisonment where fraudulent intent is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a mailbox Alberta corporation with no employees, premises, or management function for the purpose of routing bitumen trading profits through a treaty jurisdiction or to a zero-tax jurisdiction through non-arm's-length transfer prices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA can disregard the structure under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule and section 246, deny treaty relief, reclassify excess payments as deemed dividends subject to Part XIII withholding tax, and apply section 163.2 penalties for misrepresentation in a tax shelter/planning arrangement, up to CAD 1,000,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and promoters risk personal civil restitution, disgorgement of fees or profits, travel restrictions, and criminal prosecution under the Criminal Code for fraud or dishonest deprivation where the shell company is used to avoid Canadian taxes.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Purchasing penetration-grade bitumen from a related foreign affiliate above arm's-length market price, selling below arm's-length value, or allocating excessive royalty or logistics margins to offshore affiliates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA adjusts the transaction under section 247(2). If the net adjustment exceeds the greater of CAD 50,000 and 10% of gross revenue, a 10% transfer-pricing penalty applies under section 247(3). Interest, gross-negligence penalties, and retroactive reassessments may also follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve fabricated transfer-pricing studies or knowingly implement false pricing are exposed to personal penalties under section 163.2, civil claims for restitution by the company or CRA, and criminal liability for fraudulent manipulation of cross-border trade documents.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File and Unremitted Withholding Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-filing of T2, T106, T1134, or Schedule 91, and failing to withhold Part XIII dividend/royalty/interest tax on payments to non-resident shareholders or related lenders.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late-filing penalties up to 17% or 20% of unpaid tax; failure to file information returns yields daily penalties up to CAD 2,500 per form. Unremitted Part XIII withholding tax is recoverable from the payer, plus a 10% penalty for failure to withhold under section 227(9) and prescribed-rate interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under section 227.1, directors are personally, jointly, and severally liable for all unremitted withholding taxes and source deductions, including interest and penalties; CRA can issue director-liability assessments, and courts may impose travel bans or imprisonment for deliberate non-filing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using shell intermediary bank accounts, counterfeit containerized asphalt cargo documents, double-invoicing, or suspect transaction routing to obscure the source or destination of trade payments, or failing to file FINTRAC reports for large cash or suspicious transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act allows administrative monetary penalties up to CAD 1,000,000 per violation; Criminal Code money-laundering offences carry imprisonment up to 10 years and forfeiture of proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who knowingly facilitate trade-based money laundering face personal criminal liability, asset seizure and forfeiture, travel bans, disqualification from acting as directors, and piercing of the corporate veil for restitution to affected counterparties or the Crown.
